# SpreadsheetView

```csharp
public class SpreadsheetView : FrameworkElement
```

Namespace `SharpCell.Grid.Wpf` · package `SharpCell.Grid.Wpf`

Shows a SharpCell worksheet as Excel does: headers, gridlines, each cell's text as Excel formats it in the cell's style, the sheet's column widths, row heights, merged cells, frozen panes and gridlines. Cells are selected as in Excel: by clicking and dragging, by Shift with a click or the arrows, whole columns and rows from their headers or with Ctrl+Space and Shift+Space, the whole sheet from the corner or with Ctrl+A. Enter and Tab move inside a selection, the wheel scrolls and with Ctrl zooms, and Ctrl+C puts the selected cells on the clipboard as Excel pastes them. Columns and rows are resized by dragging the edges of their headers, and fitted by double-clicking them; the fill handle fills cells, and the headers have Excel's menu to insert, delete and hide them. Only the visible cells are read, so any sheet size works. The view reads cells when it paints; after changing cells or recalculating, call `UIElement.InvalidateVisual`. Sizes and frozen panes are taken when [SpreadsheetView.Worksheet](SharpCell.Grid.Wpf.SpreadsheetView.md#worksheet) is set; after changing them, call [SpreadsheetView.ReloadLayout](SharpCell.Grid.Wpf.SpreadsheetView.md#reloadlayout).

## Methods

<a id="beginedit-string"></a>
### BeginEdit(string)

```csharp
public bool BeginEdit(string? text = null)
```

Starts editing the active cell, as F2 does: with its formula or value as Excel shows it to edit, or with `text`. False when the view is read-only or has no sheet.

<a id="canceledit"></a>
### CancelEdit()

```csharp
public void CancelEdit()
```

Ends editing without changing the cell, as Escape does.

<a id="clearselection"></a>
### ClearSelection()

```csharp
public void ClearSelection()
```

Clears the content of the selected cells, as Delete does; formats and styles stay.

<a id="commitedit"></a>
### CommitEdit()

```csharp
public bool CommitEdit()
```

Enters the text being typed into the active cell, as Enter does, and ends editing; true also when nothing is being edited. A formula that does not parse keeps the editor open, with the reason shown and the caret where the formula went wrong, and gives false.

<a id="copy"></a>
### Copy()

```csharp
public void Copy()
```

Puts the selected cells on the clipboard as Excel pastes them: as text with tabs between cells, and as an HTML table with their styles. Ctrl+C and `ApplicationCommands.Copy` do it too.

<a id="cut"></a>
### Cut()

```csharp
public void Cut()
```

Cuts the selected cells, as Ctrl+X and `ApplicationCommands.Cut` do in Excel: they are copied, and the next paste moves them, formulas and formats with them; until then they stay. Escape or another change forgets the cut.


Deletes the selected cells, moving the cells below or on the right into their place, as Excel's Delete dialog does.

**Parameters**

- `shift`: Which cells take the place of the deleted ones.

<a id="paste"></a>
### Paste()

```csharp
public void Paste()
```

Pastes the text on the clipboard at the selection's top-left cell, as Ctrl+V and `ApplicationCommands.Paste` do: text copied from Excel goes in cell by cell, each read as typed. After [SpreadsheetView.Cut](SharpCell.Grid.Wpf.SpreadsheetView.md#cut), the cut cells move there instead, formulas and formats with them. The pasted cells are selected.
